title: Code prompts for decoding, meaning prompts for comprehension
statement: During word reading, prompt a stuck reader with the letters and sounds rather than 'what would make sense', and during comprehension, prompt for meaning and reasoning.
detail: An opportunities-to-respond BrainLift for early reading comprehension, sent as the playbook for a Grade 3 reading course, keeps code-based prompts out of comprehension talk and meaning-based prompts out of decoding (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md`, line 104). For word reading it follows an IES practice guide on foundational reading skills for kindergarten to grade 3 (the same file, line 209). It is a rule taken from that guide; nothing here measured it in a course.
against: The BrainLift was written for PreK to Grade 2 (the same file, line 12), and the course that adopted it leaves decoding out from Grade 3 on (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/knowledge-and-curriculum.md`, lines 209-212), so the word-reading half applies only where decoding is still taught.

evidence.quote: Keep code-based prompts out of comprehension talk and meaning-based prompts out of decoding.
During word reading, prompt with the code rather than asking “what would make sense”

citations.ref: Foorman et al. 2016, Foundational Skills to Support Reading for Understanding in Kindergarten Through 3rd Grade (NCEE 2016-4008)
